ref_extractions.title: The influence of cyber descriptive norms on immoral online behavior: The moderating role of moral conviction
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates moral conviction in online behavior through survey and experimental manipulation methods, not EEG. It does not use the openneuro_ds004067 dataset or any EEG data.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Psychology survey study with experimental manipulation about cyber norms; no EEG recording or neuroimaging.

ref_extractions.title: Moral conviction and metacognitive ability shape multiple stages of information processing during social decision-making
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original publication for dataset openneuro_ds004067. Authors Yoder and Decety (University of Chicago) conducted EEG recording during protest photo evaluation with social influence cues. The paper explicitly describes the paradigm matching the dataset's event structure (PhotoSupport, PhotoOppose, SocHigh, SocMed, SocLow, Moral_Support, Moral_Oppose, etc.).
ref_extractions.paradigm: social decision-making with protest photos and social influence
ref_extractions.epoch_params: epoch_by_event_hdf5; short stimulus markers (<2s); baseline correction; 63-channel EEG at 2000 Hz
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Condition labels based on photo type (support/oppose) and social influence level (high/med/low) or moral framing
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: 80 subjects; 81 completed EEG; 170 total participants in study; perceptual confidence task for metacognition assessment
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: EEG study with 81 participants; MFN, EPN, alpha and high beta power analyses; perceptual confidence task; protest photos with social consensus information

ref_extractions.title: Why moral convictions facilitate dogmatism, intolerance, and violence
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a theoretical essay by Jean Decety reviewing the literature on moral conviction. It cites Yoder & Decety (2022) as a reference but does not present experimental data from openneuro_ds004067 or any EEG dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Theoretical review essay drawing on 138 articles; no new experimental EEG data presented

ref_extractions.title: Impact of metacognition on attitudes toward epilepsy in medical students
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies medical students' knowledge and attitudes toward epilepsy using questionnaires. It does not use EEG, neuroimaging, or any dataset related to moral conviction or social decision-making.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Questionnaire-based survey study (N=503) about epilepsy attitudes; no neuroimaging

ref_extractions.title: Intersubject correlations in reward and mentalizing brain circuits separately predict persuasiveness of two types of ISIS video propaganda
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This fMRI study examines brain responses to ISIS propaganda videos using inter-subject correlation analysis. While it involves some Decety group members and mentions EEG preliminaries, it uses a different task paradigm, different stimuli, and fMRI not EEG. Does not use openneuro_ds004067.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: fMRI study (not EEG); ISIS Heroic vs Social video propaganda; ISC analysis; N=27 participants

ref_extractions.title: Crosstalk between delayed and immediate subjective evaluation tasks
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates dual-task paradigm effects on moral and appetitive evaluation using behavioral methods and possibly eye tracking. It does not use openneuro_ds004067 EEG dataset or any neuroimaging.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Dual-task behavioral paradigm; moral evaluation and food evaluation tasks; no EEG or neuroimaging

ref_extractions.title: Moral belief updating (MBU) as a neurocognitive and communicative process: a multidimensional perspective
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This fNIRS hyperscanning study examines moral belief updating during dyadic communication. Uses fNIRS (not EEG) with a different paradigm (moral dilemma discussion between two participants). Does not use openneuro_ds004067.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: fNIRS hyperscanning study (N=30); moral dilemma discussion; facilitator vs adjuster roles; no EEG

ref_extractions.title: AI-textuality: Expanding intertextuality to theorize human-AI interaction with generative artificial intelligence
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This applied linguistics paper introduces the concept of AI-textuality for analyzing human-AI interactions. It has no neuroscience component, does not use EEG, and is unrelated to moral conviction or social decision-making.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Theoretical linguistics paper on AI-textuality; classroom interaction data with ChatGPT; no neuroimaging

ref_extractions.title: A survey of computational methods for iconic image analysis
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper surveys computational methods for analyzing iconic images in digital humanities. It discusses computer vision and machine learning approaches to image analysis with no neuroscience or EEG content.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Survey/review paper on computational image analysis methods; no EEG or neuroimaging

ref_extractions.title: Representation in AI Evaluations
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This FAccT 2023 paper discusses representation and fairness in AI/ML evaluation datasets. It is a theoretical/ethical paper on AI benchmarks with no neuroscience content, EEG data, or connection to moral conviction research.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Conference paper on AI fairness and dataset representation; no neuroimaging or EEG

ref_extractions.title: Moral conviction interacts with metacognitive ability in modulating neural activity during sociopolitical decision-making
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This fMRI study by Cao et al. (2025) investigates moral conviction and metacognition during sociopolitical decision-making with protester evaluation tasks. Same research group and theoretical framework as openneuro_ds004067, but uses fMRI rather than EEG. The paradigm involves choosing between protester groups, similar to the EEG study's social influence paradigm. The task is related but not identical to openneuro_ds004067.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: fMRI acquisition; event-related design; parametric modulation by moral conviction level
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Which group of protesters supported more
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: fMRI study (not EEG); N=44; different modality from openneuro_ds004067 but related research from same lab; may share stimulus materials
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: fMRI study with novel decision task choosing between two protester groups; hemodynamic responses in aINS, ACC, lPFC; metacognitive sensitivity measured via perceptual task

feasibility_reason: The dataset has a well-defined event structure with clear stimulus markers for photo type (support/oppose), social influence levels (low/high/medium), and moral/non-moral cues across 80 subjects with 63-channel EEG. A relevant reference paper (10.1016/j.cortex.2022.03.008) demonstrates this exact paradigm supports EEG classification tasks with 8 condition classes involving protest photos and social consensus information.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Photo Valence Classification (Support vs Oppose)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s (relative to event onset), target_events = ["Stimulus/PhotoSupport", "Stimulus/PhotoOppose"]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| `Stimulus/PhotoSupport` | 0 | Support-framing sociopolitical protest photo |
| `Stimulus/PhotoOppose` | 1 | Oppose-framing sociopolitical protest photo |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2022.03.008
- **Kernel Notes**: Exclude admin markers (ProtestStart/End, ClipTaskStart/End, Social*/Heroic* markers, RestStart/End, S 2); response events (Resp1-7) should be excluded from stimulus-epoched analysis or handled separately for regression.

### Classical Task 2: Social Influence Level Classification (High/Med/Low)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 2.0 s (relative to event onset), target_events = ["Stimulus/SocLow", "Stimulus/SocMed", "Stimulus/SocHigh"]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| `Stimulus/SocLow` | 0 | Low agreement social influence cue |
| `Stimulus/SocMed` | 1 | Medium agreement social influence cue |
| `Stimulus/SocHigh` | 2 | High agreement social influence cue |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2022.03.008
- **Kernel Notes**: Extended 2s window captures both cue presentation and subsequent response period; can be combined with photo classification for factorial analysis.

### Classical Task 3: Moral Attitude Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.5 s (relative to event onset), target_events = ["Stimulus/Moral_Support", "Stimulus/Moral_Oppose", "Stimulus/Moral_Neutral", "Stimulus/Nonmoral_Support", "Stimulus/Nonmoral_Oppose", "Stimulus/Nonmoral_Neutral"]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| `Stimulus/Moral_Support` | 0 | Moral attitude cue - support |
| `Stimulus/Moral_Oppose` | 1 | Moral attitude cue - oppose |
| `Stimulus/Moral_Neutral` | 2 | Moral attitude cue - neutral |
| `Stimulus/Nonmoral_Support` | 3 | Non-moral attitude cue - support |
| `Stimulus/Nonmoral_Oppose` | 4 | Non-moral attitude cue - oppose |
| `Stimulus/Nonmoral_Neutral` | 5 | Non-moral attitude cue - neutral |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2022.03.008
- **Kernel Notes**: 1.5s window captures moral dimension processing distinct from photo evaluation; can be collapsed to binary moral vs non-moral classification if needed for reduced-class model.

### Classical Task 4: Full Trial Information Processing Pipeline
- **Task Type**: classification/segmentation
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 4.0 s, overlap = 0.0 s, tmin = null, tmax = null
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**: Segment-based labels capturing full trial structure from photo onset through rating response (dataset-specific mapping required)
- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2022.03.008
- **Kernel Notes**: Integrates photo + social cue + response processing; 4s window captures complete information processing pipeline; verify BIDS task mapping against OSF metadata.

### Normal Task 1: Response Rating Prediction
- **Task Type**: regression/classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 1.0 s (relative to response onset), target_events = ["Stimulus/Resp1", "Stimulus/Resp2", "Stimulus/Resp3", "Stimulus/Resp4", "Stimulus/Resp5", "Stimulus/Resp6", "Stimulus/Resp7"]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| `Stimulus/Resp1` | 1 | Rating response level 1 |
| `Stimulus/Resp2` | 2 | Rating response level 2 |
| `Stimulus/Resp3` | 3 | Rating response level 3 |
| `Stimulus/Resp4` | 4 | Rating response level 4 |
| `Stimulus/Resp5` | 5 | Rating response level 5 |
| `Stimulus/Resp6` | 6 | Rating response level 6 |
| `Stimulus/Resp7` | 7 | Rating response level 7 |

- **Evidence**: Paradigm description indicates 5-point rating scale with some variation; Resp6-7 suggest extended scale use in certain conditions
- **Kernel Notes**: Ordinal response data supports both classification and regression approaches; baseline window should capture pre-response planning phase.

### Normal Task 2: Clip Task Classification (Social vs Heroic Content)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s (relative to clip block onset), target_events = ["Stimulus/Social5start", "Stimulus/Social5end", "Stimulus/Social6start", "Stimulus/Social6end", "Stimulus/Heroic6start", "Stimulus/Heroic6end", "Stimulus/Heroic7start", "Stimulus/Heroic7end"]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| `Stimulus/Social5start` | 0 | Social content clip block start (block 5) |
| `Stimulus/Social6start` | 0 | Social content clip block start (block 6) |
| `Stimulus/Heroic6start` | 1 | Heroic content clip block start (block 6) |
| `Stimulus/Heroic7start` | 1 | Heroic content clip block start (block 7) |

- **Evidence**: Paradigm description indicates separate social influence and heroic clip task blocks; aligned with paper's investigation of social decision-making
- **Kernel Notes**: Use clip start events only for epoching; end events are for block boundary verification.

### Potential Task 1: Resting State Characterization
- **Task Type**: segmentation/analysis
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 4.0 s, overlap = 0.0 s, target_events = ["Stimulus/RestStart", "Stimulus/RestEnd"]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| `Stimulus/RestStart` | 0 | Resting block start |
| `Stimulus/RestEnd` | 1 | Resting block end |

- **Evidence**: Paradigm description indicates resting blocks were recorded
- **Kernel Notes**: Rest blocks provide baseline for noise characterization; 79 complete rest blocks available for analysis.

### Potential Task 2: Metacognitive Ability Assessment
- **Task Type**: classification/regression
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.8 s, target_events = ["Stimulus/PhotoSupport", "Stimulus/PhotoOppose"] (parametric modulation by confidence)
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**: Photo events with confidence-based parametric modulation derived from separate perceptual confidence task
- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2022.03.008 - paper explicitly mentions "perceptual confidence task for metacognition assessment" and "parametric modulation by moral conviction level"
- **Kernel Notes**: Requires super-level metadata integration with perceptual confidence scores; meta-level labels for metacognitive sensitivity may be available in supplementary data.
